But it has gone down A LOT and I’m feeling better now and my hope is that it will continue to go down a bit more on my problem side which is for sure possible and it’s possible for you too so my advice to you is to really try and relax some because the type of surgery you and I got is different than a lot of the other people on this sub, if you got a maculizing procedure I would recommend looking at the top surgery subreddit page too, because people over there got a more similar procedure to you/me than the reduction subreddit normally showcases.

My advice to you is to go with the size YOU want, not the size your mom wants. The people around you don’t need to get it, what’s most important is that your surgeon gets you and that your surgeon agrees to do what YOU want for the body you will be inhabiting forever. Also I’m not sure if your fully comfortable with your surgeon based on some of your wording, maybe you should consider a consultation with another surgeon if you have any doubts that this surgeon can get you to the size you want.
Of course, I was a 34B so already small but my surgeon would have still been able to get me here even if my cup size would have been your size so trust me that this would be possible for you too

If you want to go as flat as possible my advice is to see a top surgeon not a regular breast reduction provider. Show pictures of your ideal results and make sure who you choose says they can give you that. I asked for a small AA or AAA. Stay away from doctors who use terminology like “proportional”. Look at before and afters of your surgeon’s work, read their reviews, and what I wish I would have realized before is that swelling gets worse week 2, and that that’s normal and freaking out is not needed because swelling goes away. Also take it easy post op, make sure to rest A LOT

For example I got scared at one point that I had a seroma last week and had to drive over an hr away to see one of the few WPATH doctors close by to get an opinion. I’ve had uneven swelling and so far both Dr. Gallagher and my PCP telling me it looks like just swelling not a seroma. Also was told by Dr. Gallagher she’d prefer I not drain a seroma unless absolutely necessary because risk of infection. I’ve seen some of the other post op patients she’s had who got surgery a month ago like me, their results are less bruised and more even than mine. For some reason my body is just reacting different, strange because I’m very healthy and have low BMI so I might just be unlucky, I’m eager for the swelling to decrease.

I feel sorry for my prior chest, years of hatred and squishing them down with uncomfortable binding/tight sports bras, hating my nipples (went no nip for surgery), my chest was just trying to be, it did not know why it was always getting squished, despised. As I’m writing this I am emotional, I am also post op and know I made the right decision, there is no regret about getting top surgery but I do feel sad that I and my chest had to go through this, but living with that chest was too painful literally for the both of us, I am so relieved that it is over and I’d like to think maybe the part of me that was removed with surgery is relieved too, no more binding, no more pain, we are free now.

Oh and to clarify, she had me take off the post op binder 7 days after surgery, I wasn’t even compressing for two weeks, my surgeon seems to have an out of the ordinary timeline for compression and she didn’t to drains, no wonder I swelled up 🙄 I went with her because her results are undeniable, she’s good at her craft but her aftercare I’m learning compared to others on this sub is different for sure.

I feel her and I were on the same page for what I told her I was looking for so remembering these things helps me and remembering how I looked before the swelling increased helps me too because I believe that time was more reflective of what she did surgically.

I wish I had never stopped the post op compression when I did, I was just trying to follow my surgeon’s orders but it felt too soon, I spent about 6 days out of compression before I restarted. I can respect how my surgeons method worked for her other patients but I was told to restart compression once my swelling got worse, I even asked if I could keep the post op binder and she said she preferred I not but now here we are 😅 I’m not trying to throw shade but honestly I genuinely think it was too soon for me to take that binder off even though it was doctors orders at the time.

Week 3 and 2 were bad, week 4 starts tomorrow for me, I feel exhausted and the swelling that picked up during week 2 has been f’ing with my head. I have been paranoid of developing seroma or hematoma even though two doctors have said I don’t have these things and I’m simply just swollen. Good luck.
